text:
anya: Heads-up — trying to bring up gemma-7b-v2 for the long-context benchmarks. Quick sanity run shows a small quality regression on wiki_long and our summarization tests compared to v1. Perplexity ~+3% and ROUGE-L down ~2.1 pts on a 5k token window. wondering if this is rotary / tokenizer related.

anya: Repro steps: tokenized a handful of long examples with our HF tokenizer, then ran generate with the same prompts and temperature. Noticed some odd tokenization at code blocks — a handful of tokens map to <unk> or get split badly. Also latency is fine.

anya: Minimal dump — suspicious bits:
```
# model config snippet we saw in the converted checkpoint
rotary_scaling: 1.0  # gemma-v1 used ~0.7 in our build
rotary_base: 10000
# tokenizer claim: vocab_type: bpe and vocab_size: 50288 but merges look slightly different
```

raj: can you paste an example input + tokenized ids where it goes weird? will try to diff the merge table.

anya: pasted small example: `def foo():\n    print("π")` -> tokenized shows an extra unknown token around the unicode pi. attaching inline: `... 1234, 50288, 5, 50288 ...` (50288 is our <unk> id).

carmen: that smells like a vocab mismatch between qwen/llama style vocab and gemma. Gemma's merges sometimes include extra unicode pieces. Have you tried running the model's original tokenizer and comparing string outputs?

kevin: fwiw, we had a similar issue onboarding a qwen variant — the conversion script normalized NFKC in one pipeline but not the other. Quick check: compare `tokenizer.encode(signal, add_special_tokens=False)` from the converted tokenizer vs the original vendor tokenizer binary. If they differ, we need a merge patch or to add fallback mappings.

mike: on the rotary side, small differences in rotary_scale lead to decode drift that compounds in long contexts. In my quant experiments I saw nf4 keeps most of the head dynamics but int8-erf causes heads to saturate and you lose coherency after ~2k tokens.

kevin: example quick patches we've used: 
```python
# patch approach: remap a handful of problematic codepoints to safe tokens
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('gemma-7b-v2')
extra = ['\\u03c0']  # pi
nt = tok.add_tokens(extra)
# or load vendor merges and merge with ours (hacky but works as a stopgap)
```

anya: good — i'll diff vendor tokenizer next. On quant: mike, can you share the small comparison you ran (nf4 vs int8) for longform? a one-pager numbers table would be great.

mike: upload coming. short summary: on longform_eval (5k window)
- fp16 baseline: ROUGE-L 48.3
- nf4 4-bit: ROUGE-L 47.6 (small drop)
- int8: ROUGE-L 44.9 (bigger drop), also hallucination rate up ~6% on our QA set
CPU/latency tradeoffs are fine but quality hit for int8 is notable.

carmen: for immediate bring-up I'd prefer shipping with nf4 quant profile and a tokenizer patch. Then run a canary with 1k users (internal) and compare our prompt eval set. If tokenizer diffs remain, we should consider shipping the vendor merges as an optional tokenizer variant for this model.

anya: agreed. i'll create a canary job. plan:
- add tokenizer delta test (converted vs vendor) + small mapping fallback for odd unicode
- run nf4 quant profile on dedicated pool, run longform_eval and our regression suite (5k input)
- if perf OK, canary rollout to staging with 10% traffic for 48h

anya: command i'll run tonight: `./ci/run_eval.sh --model gemma-7b-v2 --eval longform_eval --quant nf4 --rotary_scale 0.8 --canary true`

kevin: if you tune rotary_scale, try 0.85 and 0.7 too. sometimes the best numeric match to v1 isn't 1.0 — it's model dependent. also record KV-cache consistency test (we have a tiny script `tools/kv_check.py`).

eval-bot: eval job queued (#842). dataset=longform_eval, model=gemma-7b-v2, quant=nf4, rotary_scale=0.8

deploy-bot: created canary deployment gemma-7b-v2-canary on dedicated pool (capacity 4xA10). policy: 10% staging traffic, auto-rollback on ROUGE drop > 3pts or error rate > 1.5%

raj: i'll take the tokenizer diff and make a small merge-table PR if needed. if anyone sees other unicode hiccups list them here.

anya: thanks — tagging @kevin @mike @carmen for visibility. will report back with the eval table tomorrow. :thumbsup:
